root_cause.text: The `memcg_alloc_abort_single()` function omits calling `alloc_tagging_slab_free_hook()` before freeing a slab object, leaving an outstanding allocation tag that triggers a WARNING on the next allocation when `CONFIG_MEM_ALLOC_PROFILING_DEBUG` is enabled.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `alloc_tagging_slab_free_hook(s, slab, &object, 1);` to `memcg_alloc_abort_single()`. The commit message explains that when `__memcg_slab_post_alloc_hook()` fails, the single-object free path (`memcg_alloc_abort_single`) lacks this hook, unlike the bulk free path (`kmem_cache_free_bulk`) which already includes it. The warning "alloc_tag was not cleared" shown in the stack trace confirms this mismatch.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix missing allocation tagging hook in memcg allocation abort path and micro-optimize slab pointer lookup.
intent_record.what: Added local variable 'slab' from virt_to_slab(object), inserted call to alloc_tagging_slab_free_hook before the existing slab_free_hook check, and replaced the subsequent virt_to_slab(object) call in do_slab_free with the precomputed slab variable.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the new alloc_tagging_slab_free_hook is invoked to update tagging metadata for the object being freed. Additionally, the slab pointer is computed once and reused, avoiding a redundant virt_to_slab call inside the freeing path.

This statement performs the actual freeing of the slab object. The omission of alloc_tagging_slab_free_hook() before this call leaves an outstanding allocation tag, triggering the vulnerability.

Under CONFIG_MEM_ALLOC_PROFILING_DEBUG, this omission leaves an outstanding tag that triggers a WARNING on the next allocation, as described in the root cause.

This statement performs the actual freeing of the slab object. The absence of alloc_tagging_slab_free_hook() before this call means the allocation tag is not properly cleaned up, leading to the vulnerability when CONFIG_MEM_ALLOC_PROFILING_DEBUG is enabled.
